h1: Cityview Residence, Si Racha — a small city residence on Surasaksanguan Road that punches well above its price
intro: Picture a small place right in the middle of Si Racha where you can park out front, walk a few minutes to the market and restaurants, and wake up to a breakfast buffet with Thai, Japanese, and American options — plus a rooftop terrace to head up and catch the breeze. Cityview Residence is a small 3-star residence on Surasaksanguan Road in central Si Racha, Chonburi · open since 2017 with roughly 33–35 rooms across several tiers, from Superior up to upper-floor Deluxe rooms with a jetted bathtub in the bathroom · what a lot of people mention is clean rooms, a good-looking shower and bathroom, wide balconies, free parking, and a breakfast buffet at a very light price · from about THB 850/night, rated 8.3 from 19 reviews on Trip.com and TripAdvisor 4.8 out of 5, ranked #2 of 12 small properties in Si Racha

body.html: Who Cityview Residence is for — to put it as simply as possible, Cityview Residence is a small property for anyone who wants "a clean, good-value room in central Si Racha" without paying a lot · it isn't a beachfront resort with a big pool and a sea view outside your room, and it isn't a tall, luxury chain hotel with every amenity · it's a small 3-star residence on Surasaksanguan Road in central Si Racha that focuses on being simple, clean, and within walking distance of the market, restaurants, and a downtown mall · open since 2017 with roughly 33–35 rooms, it's a small place run with a close, hands-on touch · the real reviews line up on who fits here: travelers in town for a few nights of work in the Eastern industrial zone, people stopping over in Si Racha before continuing to Pattaya-Rayong, couples or small families on a budget, and anyone driving in who wants free parking downtown · another group that says they were impressed is people who didn't expect much and got a room that "looks better inside than the building does outside," as many reviews put it · but if you're after a luxury beachfront resort, brand-new rooms in every corner, or full amenities like a pool, gym, and spa, this may not be the answer, and you should look toward Bang Saen or Pattaya instead — because the appeal of Cityview Residence is value and a central location, not luxury

Location and getting around — Cityview Residence's strong point is sitting on Surasaksanguan Road in central Si Racha, which makes it easy to walk to the town center and everyday essentials · from the property it's a short walk or drive to Pacific Park Sriracha, the downtown mall with restaurants, a supermarket, a cinema, and shops, around a 15-minute walk away · it's close to Surasak Montri Park and the Koh Loy bridge, a popular spot for views over Si Racha bay and the sunset, along with the town's shrines and markets · around the property there are Thai restaurants, Japanese restaurants, convenience stores, and markets to walk and find food, in the style of the Si Racha neighborhood that's home to many Japanese residents · for working travelers, the property is a convenient drive from the Laem Chabang industrial estates and port, as well as estates across Chonburi-Rayong · just as important, it's a short drive from Bang Saen and about 20–25 minutes from Pattaya, which makes it a good base for both work and leisure · there's a free station transfer that helps anyone arriving by public transport · plenty of reviews praise the location, that you "can walk to the market and the pier" · one small note: some reviews say there aren't many dining options within an actual walk of the property, so for more variety you may need to drive or walk farther into the town center

"The room was very clean — it looks much better inside than the building does outside, and the shower and bathroom look better than the price. Free parking out front, a short walk to the market and the pier, lovely staff. Great value for this price in Si Racha."

Room types and decor — Cityview Residence has roughly 33–35 rooms across several tiers to suit your budget and needs · the entry level is the Superior Room, a clean and simple standard room that suits a short stay or a solo traveler, followed by Superior Room with View and Superior Deluxe City View, which get more of a city view and natural light · stepping up is the Superior Deluxe with Balcony, which has its own balcony that many reviews call wide and comfortable to sit on, and the top tier is the upper-floor Deluxe with a jetted bathtub in the bathroom, for anyone who wants a more special bathroom than usual · the decor is simple in a warm, retro tone, prioritizing everyday usability over flashy design · many reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, the air-con nice and cold, and the bathroom and shower look better than the price, especially the "fancy shower" mentioned in Thai reviews · some say "it looks better inside than you'd expect from the building," a nice surprise at this price · the in-room equipment covers the standards — TV, fridge, air-con, and the necessities · to be straight about it, being a small property, some reviews note the bathrooms, whether a smell from the drain or the drainage in certain rooms, which is worth checking when you take the room — and if you find anything off, tell the team to fix it right away

Amenities, the rooftop, and extra services — even as a small property, Cityview Residence has its own complete set of amenities · a highlight many people like is the rooftop terrace, where you can head up to catch the breeze and take in the Si Racha city view in the evening, a common space that gives a small property an extra spot to relax · downstairs there's a restaurant and bar for easy meals and drinks · what pleases drivers is the free private parking, hard to come by in central Si Racha where parking space is limited · there's also free station transfer, luggage storage, taxi booking, car rental, currency exchange, and free Wi-Fi, plus room service and a front desk that's staffed throughout · to be honest, there's no pool, gym, or spa like a big hotel — anyone who needs these should set realistic expectations and pick a higher-tier property in Bang Saen or Pattaya · but for a small property downtown, having a rooftop, restaurant, free parking, and station transfer is plenty for the price · one more thing some reviews mention is the Wi-Fi signal being weak or less stable in spots, a limitation you'll find at many small properties

Food and breakfast — breakfast is something that comes up fairly often at Cityview Residence · the property has a breakfast buffet that reviews say comes in Thai, Japanese, and American styles, which is more variety than you'd expect for a small property at this price · the buffet runs in the morning from around 6:00 AM to 10:00 AM, with breakfast costing about THB 159 per adult and around THB 100 for children (or included in some packages), which is a very light price · many reviews say breakfast is fine and good value, while some note the breakfast options are fairly limited compared with a big hotel's buffet — understandable for a property of 33–35 rooms · for other meals, the central location helps a fair amount, because a walk into the Si Racha town center turns up Thai restaurants, Japanese restaurants, ramen shops, and markets to choose from, so many people head out to eat and alternate with eating in · one note some reviews mention is that there aren't many restaurants within an actual walk of the property, so for more variety you may need to drive or walk a bit farther into the center · overall, breakfast at Cityview Residence is a well-done extra at a budget price, rather than a reason to come and eat in the property as the main event

Service — service is another point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews of Cityview Residence · what guests mention often is the friendly, attentive, and helpful staff, both at a smooth, fuss-free check-in and in helping with taxi booking, car rental, or recommending where to eat and what to see in town · being a small property, the care feels close and personal, more like a guesthouse the owner runs themselves than a big, formal chain hotel — an atmosphere many people enjoy · there are all the basics: a front desk staffed throughout, room service, luggage storage, taxi booking, car rental, and station transfer · to be straight about it, with a limited team to match the property's size, small maintenance items like the bathroom or Wi-Fi may sometimes get fixed more slowly than at a big hotel, but overall service is still a strength and one reason the review scores sit in good territory

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling from Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and Wongnai, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: clean, spacious rooms with balconies nice to sit on, a bathroom and shower that look better than the price (the "fancy shower"), "it looks better inside than the building outside," comfortable beds and cold air-con, friendly and helpful staff, free parking, the rooftop terrace, varied Thai-Japanese-American breakfast, a central location within walking distance of the market and pier, and the value that many people call the main selling point · on the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is the bathroom in some rooms, both a smell from the drain and not-great drainage; next is a Wi-Fi signal that's weak in spots, fairly limited breakfast options, not many restaurants within an actual walk of the property, and some reviews mention occasional signs of insects such as ants or cockroaches, something a small property should keep on top of · on Trip.com the score is 8.3 from 19 reviews, and TripAdvisor is 4.8 out of 5, ranked #2 of 12 small properties in Si Racha, reflecting that guests are satisfied at a good level overall · these criticisms are mostly about the property's size and maintenance, fixable by picking the right room and setting the right expectations, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back

"Great value for Si Racha — clean room, cold air-con, comfortable bed · my only gripes are a slight smell from the drain in the bathroom and a weak Wi-Fi signal in spots, but the staff are lovely and parking is free. I'll come back and stay again next time."

Price and value — Cityview Residence's starting rate is about THB 850/night at normal prices, rising to around THB 1,000–1,100 for a better room or busier periods · higher-tier rooms like the Superior Deluxe with Balcony and the upper-floor Deluxe with a jetted bathtub run around THB 1,100–1,500 depending on the room type and timing · compared with other places in Si Racha, Cityview Residence feels like strong value in terms of cleanliness and location for the price, especially getting a clean room, a good-looking bathroom, a wide balcony, free parking, and a breakfast buffet in the few-hundred to low-thousand range · what adds to the value is the central location that saves both time and travel cost, plus the free station transfer and free parking, hard to find at a comparable price · if you're planning to use Si Racha as a base for work in the industrial zone, or stopping over before continuing to Pattaya-Rayong, the room and service at this price are genuinely worth it — in exchange for accepting that it's a small property with no pool or gym, and details around the bathroom and Wi-Fi to keep in mind

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoothly · one, if the bathroom matters to you, check the room's condition when you get the keys — the smell from the drain, the drainage, and the overall state; if anything is off, tell the team to move you or fix it right away · two, if you want a more special room, try choosing the upper-floor Deluxe with a jetted bathtub or a room with a balcony, which many reviews say is nice to sit on and worth the price difference · three, if you need the internet for work, have a backup plan for Wi-Fi, such as a mobile data package, because some reviews say the signal is weak in spots · four, if you drive in, free parking is a plus, but ask about the number of parking spaces ahead of time during full periods · five, when there are events in the industrial estates or on long weekends, a small property like this fills up fast — book ahead, compare prices across platforms, and pick free cancellation up front if your plans aren't set

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Cityview Residence is the best fit for anyone who wants a clean, good-value room in central Si Racha on a budget, whether you're in town for a few nights of work in the Eastern industrial zone, stopping over before continuing to Pattaya-Rayong, or visiting Si Racha for a simple trip · clean rooms, a bathroom and shower that look better than the price, a wide balcony, the rooftop terrace, free parking, a Thai-Japanese-American breakfast buffet, and friendly service make it strong value for cleanliness and location, to the point that it's not easy to find a rival in the area · if you're looking for a luxury beachfront resort, brand-new rooms flawless in every corner, or full amenities with a pool, gym, and spa, you may have to keep your expectations in check here and consider a resort in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · but for a trip where you want a clean, good-value place in central Si Racha — Cityview Residence answers that well, and it's why it earns an 8.3 from real reviews and ranks #2 among small properties in Si Racha

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Cityview Residence, Si Racha

faq.q: Where is Cityview Residence, and what can you get to from there?
faq.a: The property is at 107/2 Surasaksanguan Road, Si Racha District, Chonburi, in central Si Racha · it's about a 15-minute walk to Pacific Park Sriracha, close to Surasak Montri Park and the Koh Loy bridge, a sunset viewpoint · around the property are markets, the pier, and Thai-Japanese restaurants · it's near the Laem Chabang estates and port (~10–15 km), about 15–20 minutes from Bang Saen, and about 20–25 minutes from Pattaya · there's a free station transfer

faq.q: What's the starting price at Cityview Residence, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 850/night for a Superior Room at normal prices · there are Superior Room with View, Superior Deluxe City View, Superior Deluxe with Balcony, and an upper-floor Deluxe with a jetted bathtub in the bathroom · better rooms run around THB 1,000–1,500 depending on the room type and timing; it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Cityview Residence have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes · the property has a breakfast buffet that comes in Thai, Japanese, and American styles, open around 6:00 AM–10:00 AM, costing about THB 159 per adult (or included in some packages) · and there's free private parking in central Si Racha, plus a free station transfer and free Wi-Fi · some reviews say the breakfast options are fairly limited given the property's size

It's a great fit for people in town for a few nights of work in the Eastern industrial zone, those stopping over in Si Racha before continuing to Pattaya-Rayong, and couples or small families on a budget · you get a clean room, free parking, and a central location at a light price · if you're looking for a luxury beachfront resort with a pool and gym, Bang Saen or Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: What should you keep in mind at Cityview Residence?
faq.a: It's a small property of roughly 33–35 rooms, opened in 2017 · some reviews note a smell from the drain or the drainage in certain rooms, a Wi-Fi signal that's weak in spots, fairly limited breakfast options, and occasional signs of insects · we'd suggest you check the bathroom's condition when you get the keys and have a backup plan for the internet · but overall cleanliness, a good-looking bathroom, and service still get consistent praise

faq.q: What's Cityview Residence's review score, and is it still open?
faq.a: It's still open and operating normally · open since 2017 · the latest score is 8.3 from 19 reviews on Trip.com and TripAdvisor 4.8 out of 5, ranked #2 of 12 small properties in Si Racha · many reviews praise the cleanliness, a bathroom that looks better than the price, free parking, and the value · it's worth comparing several sources before deciding
